transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Uh… yeah, I guess they brought me in because work got weird. At the warehouse, by the forklift, I kind of froze with my arms up, and everyone was yelling, but the beeping was doing this rhythm, you know? Like the backup alarm, beep-beep, and the hand signals the guys use, I started doing them too.

And the boxes… I was moving them in these little patterns, not how they wanted. They kept telling me to stop, but I don’t know, it felt like they were supposed to go that way. So… yeah, that’s probably why I’m here.
When you started copying the beeps and hand signals, did it feel like you had to do it to stop a thought or feeling from building up inside you?

I don’t know if it was like… to stop a thought exactly. It was more like, once the forklift beeping started, and the guys were doing their hand signals, my body just kind of went with it. Like I froze there with my arms up, and then I was copying the sounds and the motions.

And the boxes, I kept putting them in these little patterns. Not the way they wanted. They were yelling, which made it harder to… I don’t know, keep track. It just felt like that’s what I was doing, like the warehouse had a pattern to it.
Before this happened, have you usually found it hard to read other people’s social cues?

I don’t know… social cues, like faces and stuff? I mean, sometimes people look annoyed and I don’t catch it right away, but I don’t know if that’s a thing or just work being loud.

Before all this, I mostly just did my job, kept moving boxes. In school there were group projects and people would do that thing where they say “it’s fine” but it’s not fine, and I never knew what they wanted— but also one time this guy in class always clicked his pen during presentations, and everyone acted like that was normal, so… I don’t know.

I guess I haven’t really thought about it like that.
Since you were a kid, have you often had strong routines or repeated movements or interests that other people thought were unusual?

Since I was a kid… I don’t really know. I mean, I had stuff I liked, like everybody has stuff, right? I don’t think anyone sat me down and said, “That’s unusual.” My mom used to get annoyed if I left toys all over the hallway, but that’s just because she’d step on them.

Repeated movements… I mean, kids do weird stuff. We had this carpet with lines in it, and I remember trying not to step on certain parts, but then the hallway at school had tiles too, and everybody was always rushing, and there was this one teacher who wore squeaky shoes, like every step was— anyway.

I don’t know if it was routines like you mean. I can’t really tell what counts.
Do you remember the whole time at the warehouse clearly, or are there parts that feel blank or missing?

I don’t know if I’d say blank. It’s kind of… pieces are there, but not like a straight movie. I remember the beeping, and the floor lines, and people yelling, and my hands being up—like I can picture that part.

But then some parts get mixed up, like I can’t tell what happened first. The boxes were in front of me and then they were in different spots, and someone was saying my name, I think. Or maybe they said “hey” and I thought it was my name. The warehouse has so many sounds that it’s hard to separate them, like when a pallet jack squeaks and then the lights hum and then you start thinking about how the aisles are numbered wrong because they skip—

Sorry. I don’t know. I remember some of it, but not clearly all the way through.
Did you have a seizure, head injury, or high fever shortly before this happened?

I don’t think so… I mean, seizure like falling down shaking? Nobody told me that happened. Head injury, I don’t remember hitting my head, but at the warehouse there’s always stuff sticking out, metal edges and pallets, and sometimes you get little bumps and don’t think about it.

High fever… I don’t know. I wasn’t taking my temperature or anything. My room gets really hot sometimes because the vent is weird, so you wake up sweating and it’s hard to tell if that’s being sick or just the apartment. But I don’t remember being, like, sick with a fever right before.
While this was happening, did it feel like something outside you was controlling your body?

I’m not sure what you mean by outside me. Like… controlled controlled? I remember my body felt kind of like it was doing things before I was thinking them, but that happens when you’re stressed, right? Like at work when the buzzer goes off and everyone moves at once, you just move.

It didn’t feel like… I don’t know. Not like a remote control or something. But everything was loud and people were staring, and then I was trying to stand still, or maybe I thought I was standing still. I keep thinking about the way the lights flicker in that place, because if you look up too long it makes your eyes feel weird.

So… I don’t know if I’d call it something outside controlling me. I can’t really tell.
Do you ever hear voices when no one is there?

I don’t… I don’t know. Like, voices meaning somebody talking clear, like standing behind me? I don’t think so. Sometimes you hear stuff in the building, like pipes or the people upstairs, and it kind of sounds like words for a second, but then it’s just the heater or someone in the hall.

At the warehouse it’s worse because the sounds bounce around, and someone can be two aisles over and it sounds like they’re right next to you. The forklifts make that backing-up sound and then the radio cuts in, and it’s hard to tell what’s what. So… I haven’t really noticed voices when no one is there, I guess. I’m not sure.
When you froze at work with your arms up, were you unable to move even though you wanted to?

I mean… yeah, I guess? That’s what they keep saying happened, that I was just standing there by the forklift with my arms up. I remember wanting to do something, but it’s fuzzy, like when you’re in the middle of the aisle and everyone’s yelling and the beeper is going and your brain starts following the sound instead of the people.

Sometimes I’d sort of copy the forklift beeping or the hand signals, and then I’d be moving boxes into these little patterns, like not the way we’re supposed to stack them. People were yelling at me to stop, and I knew they were yelling, but it didn’t connect right away. So… I don’t know if I couldn’t move, exactly, but I wasn’t moving normal even when I probably should’ve.
Right before this happened at work, had something very upsetting or overwhelming happened to you?

I don’t know… I mean, work is always kind of overwhelming, with the noise and people rushing around. But like, if you mean one big thing right before, I can’t really point to one.

It was just the usual stuff stacking up, I guess. The lights, the beeping, someone telling me to move faster—actually, the way the pallets get wrapped wrong drives me crazy because then they wobble, and everybody acts like it’s your fault even if you weren’t the one who wrapped it.

But no, I don’t think there was some huge upsetting thing right before. I can’t remember anything like that.
Do you believe anyone is trying to harm you or send you special messages?

I don’t… I’m not sure. Like, harm me how? People at work get mad, sure, but that’s different, that’s just people being annoyed because the line is backed up or the pallets aren’t right.

Special messages… I don’t think so. Sometimes signs or stuff on the radio feel like they’re sticking in my head, but I don’t know if that means anything. There’s this one safety poster by the time clock with the guy pointing, and I always notice it because the finger is drawn weird, like too long, and then I start thinking about who made it and why they picked that color. But that’s not really a message, I guess.

So… no, I don’t think anyone is trying to send me messages or hurt me. Not that I know of.
When someone moved your arms into a new position during that episode, did they stay there?

I don’t really know if they stayed there because I wasn’t… tracking it right. They told me later people were moving my arms or trying to get me to put them down, but what I remember more is standing by the forklift with my arms up, and the beeping kept catching in my head.

I was copying the beeps and some of the hand signals, I think, and then with the boxes I kept making these little patterns instead of stacking them how they wanted. Everybody was yelling, but it was like the yelling was behind glass or something.

So… maybe my arms did stay there for a bit? I can’t say it cleanly. That’s part of why they brought me in, I guess, because I kept doing weird stuff like that at the warehouse.
As a child, did other kids often say you were odd or hard to understand socially?

I don’t really know. Kids say a lot of stuff, you know? Like one day they call you weird because your shoes are wrong, next day it’s because you know the answer too fast or you don’t want to play basketball.

I remember more like… lunch tables were hard to figure out, but I don’t know if people said I was hard to understand. There was this one kid who used to chew on the strings of his hoodie, and everyone acted like that was normal, but if I didn’t laugh at the right time then suddenly I was the weird one. It didn’t make sense to me.

So… maybe sometimes? I’m not sure. I don’t remember it as a big thing people told me directly.
Before this warehouse incident, had your ability to work or take care of yourself been getting worse over the past several months?

Yeah… I guess it was getting worse. Not like all at once, though. More like people kept taking things away from me.

They stopped letting me do the forklift stuff at work, which bothered me because I was good at it before, or I thought I was. Then at school—community college—I got behind, missing things, not keeping up, and the assignments kind of stacked up like those shrink-wrapped pallets when nobody labels them right.

And I used to help at the church food bank, but I stopped going because… people said they couldn’t really count on me, or that it wasn’t safe to have me doing certain things. I don’t know, they say “safe” like it’s one word, but it means a lot of different things depending who’s saying it.

So, yes. I guess before the warehouse thing, I was already slipping.
Have you had any strong beliefs that other people said were not true?

I don’t know… “strong beliefs” how? People say things aren’t true all the time, but sometimes they mean they just don’t agree.

Like at work, if I said a pallet should be stacked a certain way, someone would say no, that’s wrong, but then later it would fall over and suddenly nobody remembers who said what. Or my mom says I remember conversations wrong, but she also forgets where she puts the mail, so…

I’m not trying to dodge it. I just don’t know what counts. I don’t think I had, like, some big belief everyone was arguing with me about. Not that I can point to cleanly.
Outside of the warehouse episode, have you had times when you were clearly seeing or hearing things that other people could not?

I don’t know. Outside of that… I mean, people hear things differently, right? Like in the dorms you hear pipes and somebody’s TV through the wall and it sounds like words sometimes, but then it’s just the building making noise.

At work too, the warehouse has all those beeps and forklifts backing up, and the lights buzzing, and once you start listening for something it kind of turns into something else. But I don’t know if that means I was hearing something nobody else could hear.

Seeing things… not really that I can point to. Sometimes shadows move weird if you’re tired, but that happens to everyone, I think. So, I guess no clear times, not outside that episode.
Before the problems over the past several months, did there used to be a time when you were functioning pretty normally?

Yeah… before all that, I think I was more normal. I mean, I had stuff going on, like everybody does, but I could do my job. They let me do the forklift then, and that was kind of a big thing because not everyone gets trusted with that, you know? You have to watch the corners and the way the pallets lean, and some guys don’t care how they wrap them—

But yeah, I was keeping up better. I was still going to community college, doing my classes, not perfect but not buried like later. And I was showing up for the church food bank shifts. People weren’t saying they couldn’t count on me back then, or acting like I was making things unsafe.

So… I guess yes. There was a time I was functioning pretty normally before it started slipping.
Have you ever felt that your thoughts were not private anymore, as if other people could hear them?

I don’t think so… I mean, sometimes people answer before I finish talking, but that’s just people being rude or thinking they know what you’re going to say. My supervisor used to do that, like he’d cut in before I explained the thing with the shrink wrap, and then the whole conversation goes sideways.

But thoughts, like hearing them out loud? I don’t know. I haven’t really noticed that. Sometimes I worry my face gives stuff away, like if I’m annoyed and trying not to show it, but that’s different, right? So… no, I don’t think my thoughts were not private like that.
Over the past several months, have you felt emotionally flat, like your face or voice showed much less feeling than usual?

I don’t know… flat how? Like not crying at stuff, or like my face just sitting there? People sometimes say I look tired, but everybody at the warehouse looks tired. The lighting in there makes everyone look kind of gray, and if you’re moving boxes for hours your face isn’t exactly doing much.

My mom used to say I had a “tone” when I answered questions, but she says that about my brother too, so I don’t know if that counts. I haven’t really been watching my own face or voice, you know? I guess I haven’t noticed it clearly.
Have there been times when ordinary things around you—like signs, colors, sounds, or patterns—felt like they had a special meaning meant for you?

Special meaning… I don’t know. Like, sometimes a sign will catch my eye, but that’s usually because it’s crooked or the colors are ugly, you know? The safety signs at work are all bright yellow and half of them are peeling, and nobody fixes them until somebody from upstairs comes through.

But meant for me? I’m not sure. I don’t think I’ve really had it like that. I notice patterns sometimes, like on boxes or the floor tiles, but I think that’s just… staring at stuff when you’re tired. So, no, I can’t say I’ve noticed ordinary things having some special message for me.

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking whether the patient’s ability to work or take care of himself had been worsening over several months, which directly concerns decline in functioning.

patient.answer:
Yeah… I guess it was getting worse. Not like all at once, though. More like people kept taking things away from me.

They stopped letting me do the forklift stuff at work, which bothered me because I was good at it before, or I thought I was. Then at school—community college—I got behind, missing things, not keeping up, and the assignments kind of stacked up like those shrink-wrapped pallets when nobody labels them right.

And I used to help at the church food bank, but I stopped going because… people said they couldn’t really count on me, or that it wasn’t safe to have me doing certain things. I don’t know, they say “safe” like it’s one word, but it means a lot of different things depending who’s saying it.

So, yes. I guess before the warehouse thing, I was already slipping.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there are persistent delusions or bizarre psychotic beliefs, which would help distinguish schizophrenia from brief psychotic, dissociative, autistic-spectrum, or organic catatonic presentations.
doctor.question: Have you had any strong beliefs that other people said were not true?

target_item.reason: The question asks about delusional or strongly false beliefs, but the provided symptom profile only covers disorganized speech, disorganized/abnormal behavior, functional impairment, and duration.

patient.answer:
I don’t know… “strong beliefs” how? People say things aren’t true all the time, but sometimes they mean they just don’t agree.

Like at work, if I said a pallet should be stacked a certain way, someone would say no, that’s wrong, but then later it would fall over and suddenly nobody remembers who said what. Or my mom says I remember conversations wrong, but she also forgets where she puts the mail, so…

I’m not trying to dodge it. I just don’t know what counts. I don’t think I had, like, some big belief everyone was arguing with me about. Not that I can point to cleanly.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there has been a sustained period of prominent psychotic symptoms, which would separate schizophrenia from brief psychotic disorder and from autism/catatonia/dissociation.
doctor.question: Outside of the warehouse episode, have you had times when you were clearly seeing or hearing things that other people could not?

target_item.reason: The question is asking about hallucinations (seeing or hearing things others cannot), but the provided symptom profile does not include hallucinations.

patient.answer:
I don’t know. Outside of that… I mean, people hear things differently, right? Like in the dorms you hear pipes and somebody’s TV through the wall and it sounds like words sometimes, but then it’s just the building making noise.

At work too, the warehouse has all those beeps and forklifts backing up, and the lights buzzing, and once you start listening for something it kind of turns into something else. But I don’t know if that means I was hearing something nobody else could hear.

Seeing things… not really that I can point to. Sometimes shadows move weird if you’re tired, but that happens to everyone, I think. So, I guess no clear times, not outside that episode.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there was a clear recent onset of catatonic/psychotic symptoms after previously normal functioning, which would help distinguish an acute transient psychotic disorder from more chronic schizophrenia or longstanding autism-spectrum traits.
doctor.question: Before the problems over the past several months, did there used to be a time when you were functioning pretty normally?

target_item.name: Functional Impairment
target_item.manifestation: I’ve lost my forklift duties, fallen behind in my community-college classes, and stopped showing up for the church food-bank shifts because people say they can’t count on me or keep things safe around me anymore.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about whether there was a prior period of normal functioning before the recent decline, which directly relates to functional impairment over time.

patient.answer:
Yeah… before all that, I think I was more normal. I mean, I had stuff going on, like everybody does, but I could do my job. They let me do the forklift then, and that was kind of a big thing because not everyone gets trusted with that, you know? You have to watch the corners and the way the pallets lean, and some guys don’t care how they wrap them—

But yeah, I was keeping up better. I was still going to community college, doing my classes, not perfect but not buried like later. And I was showing up for the church food bank shifts. People weren’t saying they couldn’t count on me back then, or acting like I was making things unsafe.

So… I guess yes. There was a time I was functioning pretty normally before it started slipping.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there are clear psychotic symptoms, especially thought broadcasting/insertion or bizarre delusional experience, to distinguish schizophrenia with catatonic features from brief psychotic, dissociative, autistic, or organic explanations.
doctor.question: Have you ever felt that your thoughts were not private anymore, as if other people could hear them?

target_item.reason: The question asks about thought broadcasting or loss of thought privacy, which is not covered by the listed symptom profiles.

patient.answer:
I don’t think so… I mean, sometimes people answer before I finish talking, but that’s just people being rude or thinking they know what you’re going to say. My supervisor used to do that, like he’d cut in before I explained the thing with the shrink wrap, and then the whole conversation goes sideways.

But thoughts, like hearing them out loud? I don’t know. I haven’t really noticed that. Sometimes I worry my face gives stuff away, like if I’m annoyed and trying not to show it, but that’s different, right? So… no, I don’t think my thoughts were not private like that.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there are persistent negative symptoms, which would help distinguish catatonic schizophrenia from brief psychotic disorder, dissociative disorder, autism-spectrum traits, or organic catatonia.
doctor.question: Over the past several months, have you felt emotionally flat, like your face or voice showed much less feeling than usual?

target_item.reason: The question is about flat affect or reduced emotional expression, but the provided symptom profiles only cover disorganized speech, disorganized/abnormal behavior, functional impairment, and duration.

patient.answer:
I don’t know… flat how? Like not crying at stuff, or like my face just sitting there? People sometimes say I look tired, but everybody at the warehouse looks tired. The lighting in there makes everyone look kind of gray, and if you’re moving boxes for hours your face isn’t exactly doing much.

My mom used to say I had a “tone” when I answered questions, but she says that about my brother too, so I don’t know if that counts. I haven’t really been watching my own face or voice, you know? I guess I haven’t noticed it clearly.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there is a sustained psychotic symptom outside the catatonic-like episode, specifically delusional perception/reference, to distinguish schizophrenia with catatonia from brief psychotic disorder, dissociative disorder, autism spectrum condition, or organic catatonia.
doctor.question: Have there been times when ordinary things around you—like signs, colors, sounds, or patterns—felt like they had a special meaning meant for you?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about ideas of reference or special meanings in ordinary stimuli, which is not covered by the provided symptom profile items.

patient.answer:
Special meaning… I don’t know. Like, sometimes a sign will catch my eye, but that’s usually because it’s crooked or the colors are ugly, you know? The safety signs at work are all bright yellow and half of them are peeling, and nobody fixes them until somebody from upstairs comes through.

But meant for me? I’m not sure. I don’t think I’ve really had it like that. I notice patterns sometimes, like on boxes or the floor tiles, but I think that’s just… staring at stuff when you’re tired. So, no, I can’t say I’ve noticed ordinary things having some special message for me.

opening_question.intent: Learn the patient's main reason for seeking psychiatric care today
opening_question.question: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The interview supports an acute psychotic episode with catatonic features: sudden freezing/posturing, echophenomena (copying beeps/hand signals), abnormal repetitive/patterned behavior, and partial disorganization/confusion around the event. A chronic neurodevelopmental pattern sufficient for Asperger syndrome was not established, and there is no clear evidence of a medical cause, seizure, delirium, persistent schizophrenia-spectrum delusions/hallucinations, or a qualifying dissociative/psychosocial trigger. Given the abrupt workplace episode with catatonic symptoms and limited evidence for a longer-standing schizophrenic syndrome, acute schizophrenia-like psychotic disorder is the best fit among the candidates.
